item.title: Medical supplies are stuck in Dubai, as clinics around the world face shortages
item.summary: The war in Iran has slowed down international shipping, much of which contains medical and humanitarian goods destined for Asia and Africa.

item.title: Trump holds a press conference after profanity-laced post on Iran
item.summary: The president has had mixed messages about how and when the U.S.-Israel-led war in Iran will end.

item.title: Iran pushes back against Trump's deadline to open the Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: Iran's top officials pushed back against a ceasefire plan and President Trump's deadline to open the Strait of Hormuz, striking a defiant tone as the warring sides traded missile attacks.

item.title: WATCH LIVE: Artemis II crew has now gone farther from Earth than any humans before
item.summary: The Artemis II astronauts have broken a record set by NASA's Apollo 13 astronauts. Once they arrive at the moon late Monday, the crew will loop about 4,000 miles from the lunar surface.

item.title: Shingles can hit younger than you think. The vaccine can prevent the painful illness
item.summary: A reactivation of the virus that causes chickenpox, the illness can be miserable. Here's what to know about early warning signs, long-term symptoms and some surprising news about the vaccine.

item.title: Supreme Court clears the way for Bannon contempt case to be dismissed
item.summary: Bannon spent four months in prison after defying a subpoena from the House Select Committee investigating the Jan. 6 attack.

item.title: Over-the-counter medication abortion? These researchers say it would be safe
item.summary: A paper in JAMA Internal Medicine adds to the growing scientific evidence that medication abortion pills would be safe to sell over-the-counter at the pharmacy. But political opposition means that possibility may not happen anytime soon.

item.title: She paid into Medicare for years. Trump's immigration policy will end her coverage
item.summary: A provision in the GOP's One Big Beautiful Bill Act will make Rosa María Carranza and an estimated 100,000 other lawfully present immigrant seniors ineligible. Her once secure retirement is in question.

item.title: These blind students say their college blocked their education. A new rule could help
item.summary: Higher education is especially reliant on computers and phones, but accessibility for people with disabilities has often been forgotten. A new federal rule could change that.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie returns to the 'Today' show months after her mother's disappearance
item.summary: Savannah Guthrie's mother, Nancy Guthrie, has not been seen since returning home from a family dinner the evening of Jan. 31.
